Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

“Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work”: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI (doi.10.1145.3411764.3445518) · paper method: COVID-era video/phone interviews prevent workflow shadowing and contextual inquiry; the findings are self-reported practices in high-stakes projects, with sampling and gender-distribution limitations.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

“Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work”: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI (doi.10.1145.3411764.3445518) · paper method: The study groups cascades into physical-world brittleness, inadequate application-domain expertise, conflicting reward systems and poor cross-organizational documentation.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

“Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work”: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI (doi.10.1145.3411764.3445518) · paper method: Between May and July 2020, the authors conduct semi-structured interviews with 53 high-stakes AI practitioners: 23 in India, 16 in the US and 14 in East/West African countries, using purposive and snowball recruitment.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

“Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work”: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI (doi.10.1145.3411764.3445518) · paper method: The authors report that 92% of their 53 interview participants experienced at least one data cascade, defined as compounding data-related events producing negative downstream effects and technical debt.

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.

  • Percentages are coded self-reports in the selected interview sample and are not population prevalence.
